title: Memory with the eyes shut
summary: Play an old piece from memory with your eyes closed, using the map in your head instead of your eyes.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: Three boxes stacked, an example map like the one redrawn from memory for an old piece: two matching sections and one different, played first with eyes open, then with eyes closed.

steps.title: Memory with the eyes shut
steps.body:
Season one taught the map of a piece: its sections, and where they repeat. This week you test whether that map lives in your head, or whether it secretly still needs your eyes to watch the hands.

1. Choose an old piece and redraw its map from memory, letters and bar numbers, with no peeking at an old map.
2. Play the piece with the page open, checking your map is right as you go.
3. Close your eyes and play the same piece, letting your hands find the keys by feel.
4. If you get lost, open your eyes only long enough to find the spot, then close them again and keep going.

A pianist who can only play while watching the hands has not really memorised the piece. Closing your eyes proves the map lives somewhere better than the eyes: in the hands themselves.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: redraw the map of an old piece from memory, no peeking
Sitting 2: play the piece with the page open, checking the map
Sitting 3: play the same piece eyes closed, opening them only when truly lost
Sitting 4: eyes closed all the way through, then once with eyes open as if recording
A different old piece, eyes closed, just the first section

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the name of the piece, then play it once through with your eyes closed, hands in the frame.
